findings.trigger_anchor: evals/harness/ablation-report.py: res["degenerate"] = bool(metric == CATCH and n > 0 and res["n_tasks"] == 1 and "ids" not in res["defect_identity"])
findings.cross_file_justification: evals/harness/ablation-row.sh (diff-touched) writes defects_missed with only a 'list of non-empty strings' check, and its --validate gate applies the same check. evals/harness/ablation-report.py (diff-touched) consumes the field as the per-defect identity vector: the degenerate check keys on 'ids' in defect_identity, so rows carrying ids switch the defect_catch_rate bootstrap (the H1 decision input) from rate mode to id mode, and the budget-matched union reads 'ids d1 … dN from defects_missed'.
findings.description: The new defects_missed field is the only per-defect identity the report has, and it changes how the pre-registered H1 catch-rate interval is built (id vectors instead of the row's rate). Neither the row writer nor --validate constrains the ids beyond 'non-empty string': no d<N> grammar, no uniqueness (['d2','d2'] passes), no bound against defects_seeded (five missed ids on a three-defect task pass), and no cross-check that defects_seeded − |missed| equals defects_caught. The validator is the schema gate for runs.jsonl, yet it will accept a row whose id list contradicts its own numeric fields, and the report's handling of unknown or duplicate ids is in the truncated hunks and cannot be confirmed from the diff.
findings.failure_mode: A grader regression, a hand-edited or re-rowed row, or a concatenated legacy file with inconsistent ids passes --validate and reaches the H1 bootstrap in id mode, where the per-defect vector may be mis-sized or over-count caught defects, silently shifting a decision-bearing interval that the row writer's own numeric fields would have contradicted.
findings.suggested_fix: In ablation-row.sh --validate (and mirror it in the row jq), when task_type is review-catch and defects_missed is non-null: require each id to match ^d[1-9][0-9]*$, require unique ids, require length ≤ defects_seeded when defects_seeded is a number, and reject when defects_caught is a number and defects_seeded − length ≠ defects_caught. In ablation-report.py, have defect_vector refuse (list the row) when an id is outside d1…dN or duplicated rather than silently coercing.

findings.anchor: #                   batch record (1.2.2) prints "Not rendered (…)" with JSON batches [] and batches_note set
findings.description: The batch record is wrapped in catch-all exception handling that copies the exception text verbatim into report.md ('Not rendered (ValueError: …); it decides nothing.') and into report.json (batches_note, batches[].note). AR-41 pins the ValueError message from int() on a manifest suite_version, and Python's int()/float()/json error strings embed the offending value, and FileNotFoundError embeds the absolute path. Reports are shared artefacts (the CHANGELOG files them under a2a/sprint-*/), so arbitrary fragments of STATUS.json, MANIFEST.json or grade.json content and host paths can end up in a published document. The exception handler itself lives in the truncated hunks; the behaviour is confirmed by the header contract and AR-41.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed or unexpected value in a batch-record input is echoed, with its surrounding path, into the committed report and JSON twin, leaking local filesystem layout or file content that the report was never meant to carry.
findings.suggested_fix: Record only the exception class and a fixed message in the rendered report (e.g. 'Not rendered (ValueError while reading STATUS.json for batch pr-2)'), log the full str(e) to stderr, and strip or relativise paths before any text reaches report.md or report.json.

findings.description: The new precision block in arm_metrics converts cost_usd with float() and no type guard, unlike the surrounding code which uses isinstance checks (and unlike the defects_caught/false_positives handling three lines above). A cost_usd that is a non-numeric string raises ValueError and aborts the whole report with a traceback, so a presentation item that is documented as 'informational, decides nothing' can prevent the decision table from being written. Separately, json.loads accepts NaN/Infinity literals, which pass isinstance(float) and propagate into true_defects/flagged_regions and then into report.json as non-standard tokens that jq consumers reject.
findings.failure_mode: One malformed row (a string cost_usd, or NaN) in a runs.jsonl that was not run through ablation-row.sh --validate turns a cosmetic section into a report-wide crash, or yields a report.json that downstream jq-based tooling cannot parse.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard cost_usd the same way as defects_caught (isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not bool, and math.isfinite), treat anything else as 0 with a note, and pass allow_nan=False to json.dump so non-finite values fail loudly at write time rather than producing invalid JSON.

findings.description: The batch record attributes each row to '<batch dir>/<arm>/<task>-t<n>-r<k>' and opens meta/pipeline.json and grade.json beneath it. The arm component comes from the row; the arm grammar ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ is enforced only by ablation-row.sh --validate, which the report does not invoke, and the report's own arm check only lists unknown arms rather than rejecting them. A row with arm '../..' would make the report enumerate and open JSON files outside the manifests tree. The GRADE_DIR pattern is also unanchored: with re.match a stray directory such as rc-01-t1-r2.bak is read as trial 1 rerun 2. The attribution code is in the truncated hunks, so this is inferred from the header contract and AR-37/AR-42; impact is read-only (only grader_version and run_id are extracted).
findings.failure_mode: A crafted or corrupted row steers the read-only tally into directories outside the batch tree, or a leftover directory with a suffix is mis-attributed to a trial, giving a wrong grader-version tally; neither affects a decision, but the report trusts an unvalidated row field as a path segment.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-apply the arm grammar (and a task_id grammar) in ablation-report.py before any filesystem path is built, resolve the candidate directory and refuse it unless it is inside the manifests root, and use GRADE_DIR.fullmatch (or anchor the pattern with ^…$) so only exact <task>-t<n>[-r<k>] names are attributed.
